evidence: NESTING (static arithmetic; every value is byte-equal to the frozen template, and task tests/test.sh is identical to the template's (diff empty)). task.toml:18 [agent] timeout_sec = 7200.0; task.toml:21 build_timeout_sec = 600.0; task.toml:27 [verifier] timeout_sec = 13200.0. Judge timeouts: gates/render/judge.toml:4 timeout = 600; gates/constraints/judge.toml:4 timeout = 600; scored/functional/judge.toml:4 timeout = 9000; scored/polish/judge.toml:4 timeout = 900; scored/visual/judge.toml:4 timeout = 900. test.sh:207 runs rewardkit with --max-concurrent-agent 1 (dimensions run sequentially, so sums apply); test.sh:213 run_suite gates 1500; test.sh:224 run_suite scored 11100. Gates: each 600 < 1500 and sequential sum 600+600 = 1200 < 1500 (300 s slack). Scored: each of 9000/900/900 < 11100 and sum 9000+900+900 = 10800 < 11100 (300 s slack). Budgets: 1500 + 11100 = 12600 < 13200 (600 s slack for copy, launch, liveness, score.py). Internal-sheet reading 'sum of judges < verifier': 600+600+9000+900+900 = 12000 < 13200. Liveness: test.sh:116-122 polls 120 x 0.25 s (~30 s nominal; each probe may add up to 2 x 2 s urlopen timeouts, worst case ~510 s, which consumes most of the 600 s outer slack only for an app that hangs connections without answering, in which case test.sh exits 0 with the zero reward at :123-125). Restart helper uses the same loop inside restart_mcp.py HELPER_TIMEOUT_SEC = 55 (tools/restart_mcp.py:11); via-solve.log shows the golden restart group PASS. Timed steps are bounded: functional prompt.md:21 15000 ms poll + 2000 ms settle per attempt, at most 3 attempts, in one browser_run_code_unsafe action (Colderwater lessons 7/14 pattern present). Agent side: environment/Dockerfile (identical to template) apt-installs 4 packages and npm installs express@5.1.0 + better-sqlite3@12.4.1 (prebuilt for node22 bookworm), comfortably under build_timeout_sec 600; agent 7200 s is the template value and the Colderwater handoff records builders finishing in 5-10 min. No timeout was changed, so no authorization record is needed. LONG ENOUGH (unmeasured): the template's functional dimension has 2 criteria in 9000 s; this task's has 44 (grep -c '[[criterion]]' = 44) in one batched claude-code session with the same 9000 s, about 204 s per criterion, many needing several independent browser contexts, sign-ins as multiple personas, timed live-update observations with up to three attempts, bulk/undo/stale-write sequences, paged history, and a final single-use restart that re-reads every recorded fact (prompt.md:59 'Restart LAST'). raw-evidence-index.json scope says verbatim 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent', and each artifact says 'Not a configured judge run ... or judge-duration measurement'. The 26-group scripted Playwright driver is not LLM judge duration (REVIEW_POLICY). Whether 9000 s suffices for glm-5.3-flashx driving 44 criteria is therefore not measured; nesting passes, but the 'long enough' half cannot be credited. Per SKILL 'Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass' and REVIEW_POLICY 'Workload is measured, not inferred from a timeout number', the verdict is Not exercised with risk=true. Severity P1 is the consequence if the risk materialises, not a demonstrated defect. Colderwater lessons checked for this row: 11 (judge infra timeouts zero a dimension) bears directly: a functional timeout zeros functional, which fails the 0.05 functional floor (scoring.toml [floors]) and zeros the whole reward even for the golden. 7/14 timing-step bound verified present. 10: assembled functional prompt ~21.7 KB prompt.md + ~26 KB criteria + 1.9 KB app_context, about 50 KB < 128 KB (noted only). 19: a scripted harness exists but measures golden behaviour, not judge time. 21: no rerun-until-green issue applies. Broken-app probe: a fast-failing stub finishes early and is graded normally; a suite timeout writes zero (test.sh:213/:224 exit 0 after the zero record), so timeouts cannot give a broken app false credit. Conforming-alternative probe: a correct but slower app (live updates landing at 10-14 s, slower page loads) lengthens every timed step and multi-context sequence; if cumulative judge time crosses 9000 s, the functional dimension is lost and the reward is 0. A correct app could fail purely on evaluator budget. This counterexample is plausible but unmeasured, so it is recorded as a risk, not a Fail.
counterexample: Unmeasured hypothetical, not a demonstrated failure: a conforming HireOps app whose live updates arrive near the 15 s window and whose screens load slowly pushes the 44-criterion batched functional session past its 9000 s timeout (the template value, sized for 2 criteria). RewardKit zeros functional, the 0.05 functional floor fails, and the correct submission scores 0.
suggested_fix: Before clearance, run the full configured verifier (test.sh with claude-code + z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx) on the golden at least once and record per-dimension wall time against 600/600/9000/900/900. If functional uses more than ~70% of 9000 s, reduce redundant browser work and criteria with matching public scope, or obtain explicit authorization for a justified budget change below five hours with the measured reason recorded.
